# RFC-0001: Specification Overview And Authority Map

> **Version:** 0.64.2 | **Status:** normative | **Phase:** stable
> **Owners:** @Zihua Wu

---

## 1. Summary

### [RFC-0001:C-SUMMARY] Summary (Informative) <a id="rfc-0001c-summary"></a>

InferLab runs reproducible LLM inference experiments: a versioned workspace fixes the shareable baseline, stacks own framework realizations, independently launchable servers own serving intent and cases, recipes compose one server with one workload suite, local bindings supply concrete machine placement, and every execution writes durable file-first evidence. This document is the specification entry point and maps each contract area to its owning RFC.

**Authority map:**

- RFC-0002 — workspace, stack, and local-placement authority: revision and source identity, local bindings and dirty-workspace policy, Pixi lifecycle, stack realization checks, ad-hoc execution, and runtime caches.
- RFC-0003 — server, recipe, and runtime execution: server and case composition, one resolved authority, long-running and closed-loop workflows, canonical Engine and frontend topology, per-role parallelism, independent Gateway and P/D Router backends, and fused P/D frontend binding.
- RFC-0004 — measurements and toolchains: Eval and Bench semantics, InferLab-owned measurement toolchains, and workload profiling.
- RFC-0005 — evidence: immutable resolved execution records, runtime evidence, and operator journal.
- RFC-0006 — adapter protocol version 7 and independently distributed integration packages.
- RFC-0007 — stack-based runtime image production, validation, and container launch facts.
- RFC-0008 — agent plugin distribution.
- RFC-0009 — runtime time-bound semantics: operation budgets, nested attempt bounds, measurement-case deadlines, deliberately unbounded operations, and cleanup grace.
- RFC-0010 — view-only workspace TUI: navigation across declared definitions, current CLI operations, records, and bounded live observations.
- RFC-0011 — public product and documentation website: content authority, current public-snapshot presentation, static validation, and GitHub Pages delivery.
- This document — cross-cutting operator progress and output streams (RFC-0001:C-OPERATOR-PROGRESS), error codes (RFC-0001:C-ERROR-CODES), and license-notice retention (RFC-0001:C-LICENSE-RETENTION).

**Scope:** The specification covers externally observable configuration authority, command semantics, protocol boundaries, and evidence. It does not prescribe crate layout, private implementation types, arbitrary workflow graphs, registry publication, or compatibility with configuration and record schemas predating this contract.

**Conformance language:** MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, and MAY are normative keywords with their customary specification meaning across every RFC in this set.

**Rationale:** The contract fixes the operator capabilities proved necessary — fixed-workspace installation, direct and closed-loop server lifecycle, heterogeneous multi-role placement, measurement, images, profiling, and durable evidence — while keeping production-service supervision, provider indirection, universal workflow planning, and generic measurement dependencies out of the serving stack. Topic RFCs own and version their areas independently.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0001:C-ERROR-CODES] Error Code Registry (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-error-codes"></a>

InferLab reports every runtime failure under exactly one error code. When a command fails, the CLI MUST exit nonzero and MUST write one diagnostic line to stderr of the form `error[<code>]: <message>`. Codes are the machine-branchable contract; message text is guidance and MAY change between releases. Command-line usage errors (argument parsing) are reported by the argument parser and are outside this registry.

**Registry.** The leading digit groups codes by failing subsystem.

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| E1001 | Workspace discovery failed: no workspace manifest found from the start directory upward. |
| E1002 | A required file could not be read. |
| E1003 | Configuration could not be parsed or serialized. |
| E1004 | Configuration is invalid: well-formed input that violates the contract. |
| E1005 | A server override value is invalid. |
| E1006 | A git operation failed. |
| E1007 | The committed Pixi environment lifecycle failed: realization, launch, restoration, or an unusable environment. |
| E1008 | The measurement toolchain failed: unsupported platform, installation, verification, launch, or a missing toolchain. |
| E2001 | A framework integration failed: launch, transport, timeout, protocol violation, or rejection. |
| E3001 | Placement failed: a machine binding provides fewer devices than the server requires. |
| E4001 | A closed-loop run (recipe, Bench, or image build) failed after finalizing its record; the message names the record id. |
| E4002 | A server lifecycle operation, the built-in proxy, or profiling failed. |
| E4003 | An image build or image selection was rejected. |
| E5001 | Server record access, decoding, or encoding failed. |
| E5002 | A workspace operation observation could not be encoded, published, updated, or removed. |
| E6001 | A scratchpad journal operation failed. |
| E7001 | An agent plugin operation failed. |
| E8001 | An ad-hoc environment execution was rejected or could not launch the operator command. |
| E9001 | Command output could not be written or encoded. |

**Stability.** The registry is append-only. A published code MUST keep its meaning across releases and MUST NOT be reused for a different meaning. A new failure condition MAY join an existing code only when it matches that code's stated meaning; otherwise a new code MUST be added. Consumers MAY branch on codes and MUST NOT need to parse message text.

*Since: v0.58.0*

### [RFC-0001:C-LICENSE-RETENTION] License Notice Retention (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-license-retention"></a>

Every distributed InferLab artifact MUST retain the project's license notice text; a license identifier or SPDX expression alone does not satisfy retention.

Per artifact form:

- Packages — Python wheels and sdists, and published crates — MUST contain the license file, byte-identical to the repository text, and a build or packaging gate MUST fail when a package copy drifts from that text or a built artifact lacks it.
- The agent plugin package MUST pack the license file, and packaging MUST fail when it is absent.
- The binary MUST embed the notice and print it with `inferlab license`, so a bare binary download retains it with no companion file.
- Each release MUST publish the license as a first-class asset for human discovery.

**Rationale:** The license's own condition attaches to copies of the software, so retention holds by construction in every artifact form rather than by anyone remembering to bundle a file: index installs, release downloads, plugin installs, and bare binary copies each carry the notice through the artifact itself.

*Since: v0.59.0*

### [RFC-0001:C-OPERATOR-PROGRESS] Operator Progress And Output Streams (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-operator-progress"></a>

InferLab MUST preserve stdout as the command result stream. Progress MUST NOT appear on stdout for a command that returns a machine-readable or human-readable InferLab result.

Progress governed by this clause MUST be emitted as complete newline-terminated text lines on stderr. Its meaning MUST NOT depend on cursor control, animation, color, or terminal detection. Progress wording beyond the facts required by this clause is operator guidance and MAY change between releases; callers MUST use final command output and [RFC-0001:C-ERROR-CODES](../rfc/RFC-0001.md#rfc-0001c-error-codes), not progress text, for machine branching.

`workspace lock`, `toolchain install`, non-dry-run `serve start`, `serve stop`, non-dry-run `recipe run`, non-dry-run `bench`, and non-dry-run `image build` MUST report their first phase before waiting on a lock or starting their first potentially blocking external operation. Afterward they MUST report each applicable phase when it begins.

`stack status`, `serve status`, `serve logs`, `scratchpad note`, `scratchpad show`, and the dry-run forms of `serve start`, `recipe run`, `bench`, and `image build` MAY remain quiet when they complete within ten seconds. If one of those commands has not completed within ten seconds, it MUST report its current phase no later than the ten-second point and MUST report each subsequent phase when it begins.

A reported phase that remains active for ten seconds MUST emit a heartbeat no later than ten seconds after that phase was first reported. It MUST continue to emit heartbeats no more than thirty seconds apart until the phase ends. Each heartbeat MUST identify the command, the current phase, and the elapsed duration of that phase.

When a phase processes a bounded collection, progress MUST identify the current item and its ordinal position and total when those facts are known. A readiness heartbeat MUST include the most recent readiness failure when one exists. A lock-wait heartbeat MUST identify the contended lock.

The governed commands MUST expose these operator phases when they apply:

- `workspace lock`: base-lock production, staged base installation, authoritative full-lock production, and restoration after failure or interruption;
- `toolchain install`: installation-state inspection, writer-lock waiting, incomplete-installation replacement, Pixi installation, Eval verification, and Bench verification;
- `serve start`: resolution, local and remote preflight, process launch, and readiness for each resolved process;
- `serve stop`: profiler finalization, process termination, container removal, and log synchronization for each resolved process;
- `recipe run`: resolution, server startup, each Eval, each Bench case or adaptive probe, profiler finalization when selected, and server cleanup;
- `bench`: resolution and admission, each Bench case or adaptive probe, and profiler finalization when selected;
- `image build`: resolution plus the record, package-build, assembly, inspection, export, and validation phases required by [RFC-0007:C-IMAGE-BUILD](../rfc/RFC-0007.md#rfc-0007c-image-build);
- `scratchpad note` and `scratchpad show`: journal-lock waiting.

When a command creates a durable record, the next progress line after creation MUST identify the record identifier and record directory, and it MUST be emitted before any subsequent potentially blocking operation. When a durable log path exists before a potentially blocking external operation starts, that operation's phase report MUST include the log path.

Progress is ephemeral operator guidance. It MUST NOT replace authoritative execution records, command evidence, result artifacts, or failure diagnostics, and it MUST NOT be reconstructed into those artifacts as a second authority.

`inferlab run` MUST NOT emit wrapper progress after the operator command starts, because that command owns its stdout and stderr under [RFC-0002:C-ADHOC-EXECUTION](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-adhoc-execution). Fast local-only commands for workspace display and license output have no progress requirement. `agent install`, `agent update`, `agent uninstall`, and `agent doctor` have no phase or heartbeat requirement under this clause; their result and error behavior remains governed by [RFC-0008:C-AGENT-PLUGIN](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-agent-plugin) and [RFC-0001:C-ERROR-CODES](../rfc/RFC-0001.md#rfc-0001c-error-codes).

The terminal InferLab result and the error-code behavior of [RFC-0001:C-ERROR-CODES](../rfc/RFC-0001.md#rfc-0001c-error-codes) remain unchanged. A progress line MUST NOT be formatted as a terminal `error[<code>]: <message>` diagnostic.

**Rationale:** Long InferLab workflows intentionally capture protocol output and preserve external-tool and experiment output in durable logs, while stdout carries one final report. Without a separate progress contract, a correctly advancing installation, readiness wait, measurement matrix, or cleanup is indistinguishable from a stalled command. Semantic phases, bounded elapsed-time heartbeats, and early record and log discovery make the operation observable without corrupting stdout, duplicating record authority, exposing protocol streams, or inventing unreliable percentages and completion estimates.

*Since: v0.63.0*

Authority map names local bindings and dirty-workspace policy (RFC-0002), image-backed and external-image launches (RFC-0003), adapter package distribution (RFC-0006), and container launch facts (RFC-0007)

### v0.56.0 (2026-07-05)

Restructured into the specification's meta document: the eighteen contract clauses moved to topic RFCs 0002-0008 (workspace/environments, recipes/execution, measurements/toolchains, evidence/journal, integration protocol, images, agent plugin); this RFC now holds the overview, authority map, scope, and conformance language

### v0.55.0 (2026-07-05)

Public-readability sweep of clause prose: generation labels, internal episode names, and development narration removed; rationales argue from mechanism in public terms; no normative behavior change

### v0.54.0 (2026-07-04)

Added C-AGENT-PLUGIN: the CLI provides agent plugin install/update/uninstall/doctor over the repo-shipped package, with validate-before-invoke, loud failures, isolation from the experiment contract, and one JSON report per operation

### v0.53.0 (2026-07-04)

C-EVIDENCE: non-dry-run server records identify the assigned GPU hardware (model, memory, UUID) and driver version per hosting machine, probed at launch through the launch path; a failed probe fails the launch loudly

### v0.52.0 (2026-07-04)

Reworked C-SCRATCHPAD-JOURNAL: the thread/active model is replaced by one append-only journal per workspace with optional explicit per-entry topics, zero-setup appends, and a tail-first default view

### v0.51.0 (2026-07-04)

C-WORKSPACE-AUTHORITY: the workspace source exclusion enumeration gains the .inferlab scratchpads subtree, matching C-SCRATCHPAD-JOURNAL's source-identity exclusion

### v0.50.0 (2026-07-04)

Added C-SCRATCHPAD-JOURNAL: operator scratchpad journal of append-only entry threads on the record-identifier time axis, excluded from source identity

### v0.49.0 (2026-07-04)

C-WORKLOAD-PROFILING: managed-option rejection covers abbreviated long forms — any strict prefix of a managed long option name, which either resolves to the managed option or is an ambiguity

### v0.48.0 (2026-07-04)

C-WORKSPACE-AUTHORITY: link-resolved judgment substitutes only through digest-visible links; a digest-visible target resolving onto or through a machine-local link is rejected naming the starting link, its target, and the machine-local link

### v0.47.0 (2026-07-04)

C-WORKLOAD-PROFILING: standalone - or -- tokens in escape option lists are rejected at workspace load — they end option parsing and displace the managed argv tail into positionals of the wrapped command

### v0.46.0 (2026-07-04)

C-WORKLOAD-PROFILING: managed-option rejection covers attached short-option-value forms; escape environment keys are POSIX identifiers rejected at load; the rendered environment prefix terminates option parsing before the first assignment

### v0.45.0 (2026-07-04)

C-WORKSPACE-AUTHORITY: symlink containment covers the digested worktree (root minus .git, source exclusions, and git-ignored directories) rather than declared source-set subtrees; targets resolving through enumerated links are judged link-resolved with cycles rejected; rejection evidence names the source set only when one declares the link

### v0.44.0 (2026-07-04)

C-WORKLOAD-PROFILING: profiler escape inputs on serve profiles and roles — split launch/start option lists spliced ahead of the managed argv tails, dedicated executable/trace/sampling/context-switch fields, an env map with launch-inheritance scope, role-into-profile merge semantics, load-time managed-option rejection, and raw-plus-effective record evidence

### v0.43.0 (2026-07-03)

Capture-armed readiness waits are unbounded (terminating by success, process-group exit, or interruption); window-closing control failures are adjudicated by report coverage; window-control response deadlines honor the serve-profile fact capture_control_deadline_seconds, default 60

### v0.42.0 (2026-07-03)

Ignored source-set links are machine-local state bound by containment alone (absolute targets judged against this root); digest-visible links keep the full identity-coverage requirement

### v0.41.0 (2026-07-03)

Source-set symlink containment covers every effective worktree link regardless of tracking state and requires identity-covered targets: within the root, outside .git and the workspace source exclusions, and not git-ignored per the target's owning repository; dangling internal targets stay permitted

### v0.40.0 (2026-07-03)

Declared source sets must not contain tracked symbolic links whose targets are absolute or lexically escape the workspace root; rejected when the snapshot claims source identity, with workspace-internal relative links remaining permitted

### v0.39.0 (2026-07-03)

Strengthen the symlink rejection to path components: no component of the workspace configuration paths (including the .inferlab directory itself) and no component of a declared source-set path may be a symbolic link — the source digest records link text rather than target content

### v0.38.0 (2026-07-03)

Require the root workspace file, the workspace.d directory, and every fragment to be regular filesystem entries: a symbolic link in any of those positions is rejected at load because the source digest records link text rather than target content

### v0.37.0 (2026-07-03)

Name the multi-file workspace composition contract: root workspace.toml plus workspace.d fragments compose as a disjoint union of identifier-keyed definitions; two-file identifier collisions are rejected naming both files; schema_version and workspace-global scalars live only in the root file

### v0.36.0 (2026-07-03)

Name the measurement client result envelope version contract: clients write version 1; the measurement runtime rejects an Eval or Bench result whose envelope version it does not support (codifies the existing bench rejection, extends it to eval)

### v0.35.0 (2026-07-03)

POSIX-identifier pass-through names; the no-value guarantee is the remote channel's

#### Changed

- C-IMAGE-BUILD — declared pass-through names must be POSIX shell identifiers (the launch scripts splice them into shell parameter references)
- C-RUNTIME-WORKFLOWS — the value-never-enters-the-plan guarantee is scoped to remote launches; local launches compose the invoking environment into the recorded env map under the unredacted-records posture

### v0.34.0 (2026-07-03)

Pass-through values flow from the launching machine; launch failures remove their containers

#### Fixed

- C-RUNTIME-WORKFLOWS — declared pass-through values flow into the container from the launching machine's environment via shell references; the value never enters the plan, the recorded command, or the launch script text
- C-RUNTIME-WORKFLOWS — a launch failure after the container may already exist attempts the same confirmed removal with the assigned name on its launch machine

### v0.33.0 (2026-07-03)

Server containers carry a container handle; cleanup confirms removal on the launch machine

#### Added

- C-RUNTIME-WORKFLOWS — every containerized server process carries a resolver-assigned container name in the recorded launch command; cleanup confirms the container's removal on its launch machine (already-absent is the confirmation) and never claims verification while a known container's removal is unconfirmed

### v0.32.0 (2026-07-02)

Multi-machine external-image serving: per-machine presence probes, machine-scoped substitution facts, SSH container handles

#### Added

- C-RUNTIME-WORKFLOWS — external-image selections may resolve to multi-machine placements; presence verified by read-only probes on the controller and every launch machine, missing image fails naming the machine and exact pull command; Inferlab never distributes images
- C-RUNTIME-WORKFLOWS — remote containerized launches skip the remote workspace-realization check; machine-scoped launch facts (container user identity, pass-through reporting) resolve against each launch machine and enter the record's evidence; SSH container processes carry remote host-process handle and cleanup semantics

#### Changed

- C-RUNTIME-WORKFLOWS — the image build record selection keeps the single-host gate and its rejection names the distribution boundary

### v0.31.0 (2026-07-02)

Declare per-machine container hardware facts (devices, memlock, capabilities) lowered by the containerized substitution

#### Added

- C-IMAGE-BUILD — local bindings may declare per-machine container hardware facts (host device paths, unlimited pinned-memory ulimit, Linux capabilities); operator-declared, never auto-detected, load-validated, never privileged; runtime launch facts excluded from image content and closures
- C-RUNTIME-WORKFLOWS — the containerized substitution lowers declared container hardware facts into every server container for image-backed and external-image launches; the adapter container receives no device or capability grants beyond its declared workaround device

### v0.30.0 (2026-07-02)

Declared external serving images: digest-pinned, integration-claimed workspace facts consumable by serve start and recipe run as an explicitly not-qualified realization — no pull, explicit command override, in-image lowering with an observed framework version, cache namespaces keyed on the external digest

### v0.29.0 (2026-07-02)

C-RUNTIME-WORKFLOWS: local bindings may declare an image-adapter deadline and a degraded-host workaround device, both load-validated; the adapter container requests no device when none is declared

### v0.28.0 (2026-07-02)

C-RUNTIME-WORKFLOWS: image-backed placement rejection precedes network resolution and remote-machine preflight, and a failed or timed-out in-image integration invocation must not leave its container running

### v0.27.0 (2026-07-02)

Image-backed resolution executes integration lowering against the image realization (no locally installed serving environment required), rejects incompatible selections before any integration invocation, keys runtime JIT cache namespaces on the image identity, and passes resolver- and integration-set process environment explicitly instead of inferring it from ambient values

### v0.26.0 (2026-07-02)

C-RUNTIME-WORKFLOWS: image-backed resolution rejects launches whose server processes carry profiling capture targets until an in-container profiler contract exists — a host-side profiler wrapping the container client would claim a server profile it never took

### v0.25.0 (2026-07-02)

C-RUNTIME-WORKFLOWS: serve start and recipe run accept an image build record selection; image-backed launches reuse the containerized substitution with compatibility rejections at resolution, preserve image identity and both workspace revisions in server records, and leave manual Bench semantics unchanged

### v0.24.0 (2026-07-02)

Per-machine launch preflight and attributable in-image check evidence

#### Changed

- C-ENVIRONMENT-CHECKS — launch preflight covers each distinct machine realization, evidence records the examined machine, infrastructural check failures still finalize the consuming record
- C-PIXI-ENVIRONMENT-LIFECYCLE — declared checks run against the controller and each remote machine realization before any process launches
- C-IMAGE-BUILD — failed entry checks finalize the record and emit the failed report, in-image checks leave attributable per-check results in the builder log even on failure, the image identity enters assembly evidence the moment the builder returns it

### v0.23.0 (2026-07-02)

Environment realization checks and image postprocess

#### Added

- C-ENVIRONMENT-CHECKS — workspace-declared realization checks and image postprocess steps, one declared set executed per realization, fix ownership follows realization ownership

#### Changed

- C-IMAGE-BUILD — entry checks against the local realization before package builds, in-Dockerfile postprocess and check layers via the entrypoint so image existence implies checks passed, scripts enter the frozen context and the content closure, check outcomes in image records
- C-PIXI-ENVIRONMENT-LIFECYCLE — declared checks run as preflight before server launch from the locally installed environment

### v0.22.0 (2026-07-02)

Release-owned distribution of workspace-side Python packages

#### Added

- Adapter SDK and integrations materialize from the release into a workspace-relative toolchain path; committed manifests reference only that path

### v0.21.1 (2026-07-02)

Clean build environments carry a fixed system-utility path suffix

#### Added

- The clean build environment includes a constant system-utility PATH suffix; git and CMake helpers need the base userland

### v0.21.0 (2026-07-02)

Seventh-round review: close the build input closure

#### Added

- Reuse key covers editable packages outside the source set by content identity
- Wheel builds run in a clean environment; ambient shell state is not a build input

### v0.20.0 (2026-07-02)

Feature-composed activation projection with verified precedence

#### Added

- Feature-scoped activation env is composed per pixi's verified precedence instead of rejected; only binding activation scripts fail resolution

### v0.19.2 (2026-07-02)

Scope unmodeled-activation rejection to branches binding the selected environment

#### Added

### v0.19.1 (2026-07-01)

Unmodeled activation branches rejected at image resolution

#### Added

- Feature-scoped activation and activation scripts fail image resolution loudly instead of being silently missed

### v0.19.0 (2026-07-01)

Sixth-round review: concurrency-safe immutable cache publication, environment-scoped reuse key, no retained payloads, cleanup evidence

#### Added

- Package reuse keyed on the selected environment's locked closure and projected activation instead of whole-file manifests
- Cache publication no-clobber with private staging; races adopt the published artifact
- Successful assemblies retain no package payloads; cleanup failures preserved in evidence alongside primary failures

### v0.18.0 (2026-07-01)

Fifth-round review: builder-scoped platform batches, frozen build contexts, atomic package publication, audit-failure evidence

#### Added

- Resolution scopes assembly to builder-producible platforms; skipped platforms reported with reasons, never planned or failed; all-unproducible declarations fail resolution
- Build contexts frozen and minimal; scratch, source copies, and logs live outside; sanitized-copy cleanup failure fails the assembly
- Package cache publication atomic; no duplicate package payload retained in the record
- A mutation audit that cannot execute fails the assembly preserving the build outcome

### v0.17.1 (2026-07-01)

Fourth-round review: enforce name-reference pass-through, unconditional mutation audit, single-reference redirects

#### Added

- pass_env names validated at binding load; absent variables reported at launch
- Mutation audit runs regardless of build outcome, preserving the build failure
- Multi-reference activation values rejected at redirect time

### v0.17.0 (2026-07-01)

Third-round review: scoped credential promises, runtime pass-through env, observation evidence, mutation detection, context procedure identity, progress reporting

#### Added

- Credential guarantee scoped to Inferlab-known facts; name exclusion is best-effort for committed content; no secret-scanning promise
- Local bindings may declare per-machine container pass-through env, passed by name reference only
- Resolution probes recorded as observations in the resolved plan; pre-execution persistence required only for state-affecting commands
- Package builds use a sanitized view with redirected activation references; workspace mutation is detected and fails the assembly
- Content closure includes a context-generation procedure identity; image build reports record identity and phase progress on the diagnostic stream

### v0.16.0 (2026-07-01)

Second-round review hardening for runtime-image production

#### Added

- Package reuse requires unchanged target platform and build-procedure identity in addition to source identity, lock, and generator identity
- The package build-procedure identity enters both the reuse key and the image content closure
- Portability guarantee scoped to generated text and image metadata; credential-named activation variables excluded from the projected entrypoint
- Exported archive paths unique per producing record; native builder commands persisted durably before execution
